newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold exchange trade heavy on arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold exchange trade heavy on arbitrage.

text.p: The Istanbul gold exchange saw heavy trade on Wednesday with 2,230 kilos, the second highest volume ever and well up on Tuesday's 1,860 kilos, as banks engaged heavily in arbitrage transactions, dealers said.
Daily record volume was seen on January 8 with 2,570 kilos.
Gold closed easier at $348.00 an ounce and 1,424,000 lira per gram compared to $352.00 and 1,436,000 lira on Tuesday following weaker prices on world markets.
"We can say that nearly all of today's trade was due to arbitrage by the banks. Other than that, there wasn't much demand on the free market," one dealer said.
The Turkish lira eased to 127,110 to the dollar, from 126,735 on Tuesday.
Of the day's trade, 1,000 kilos changed hands in the morning session and the remainder in the afternoon - 60 percent of trade was conducted in lira terms.
